title: Emerging-model tributary tracker and alert procedures
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, reproducible tracker and alerting protocol for small but fast-moving model entrants and forks ("tributaries") that could affect Redwood’s hosted and dedicated offerings. The tracker should fuse telemetry (latency/cost observations), public signal (release notes, GitHub commits, model cards), and customer-reported anomalies into an operational alert that highlights urgency, likely impact vector (latency, cost, API compatibility), and recommended next steps for PM/Engineering/SE teams.
goals: Detect emergent model variants within 72 hours of public availability or credible signals
Surface clear actionability for PM, SRE, and Solutions within the alert payload
Reduce manual triage time per emergent model from days to <4 hours on average
Provide traceable provenance links and a minimal reproducible test case for downstream engineering experiments
success_metrics: Mean time to first-triage for emergent-model signals <= 4 hours
Fraction of alerts with recommended next-step created by PM >= 90%
Reduction in surprise-production-deploy incidents attributable to untracked model variants by 60% within 3 months
Number of emergent-model entries seeded into the model-scout inventory per month >= 6
tasks: Design a 5-field alert schema (signal_source, confidence, impact_vector, recommended_next_step, provenance_links)
Prototype a nightly job that scrapes model registries and GitHub releases for keywords and forks
Instrument quick telemetry probes against suspect model endpoints (latency/cost microbench) using sandbox credits
Create triage playbook docs in Confluence and a lightweight issue template for Engineering
Define escalation thresholds and rota for on-call PM/SE review
Build a minimal dashboard tile in Console for active tributary alerts and historical provenance
stakeholders: Data Team observability contact: Omar Farouk

open_questions: What minimum telemetry budget can we spend per candidate before returning a false-positive cost blowup?
Should tributary alerts surface in customer-facing status pages or remain internal until validated?
Is there a legal/privacy constraint around scraping model artifacts from certain registries?
acceptance_criteria: Nightly scraper runs and produces alerts for at least 80% of known public model releases in a 7-day window
An alert contains the 5 required fields, at least one provenance link, and a microbench snapshot when applicable
Confluence triage playbook published and linked from the alert payload
Dashboard tile shows active alerts and a one-month timeline of resolved tributaries
notes: Design should prioritize low false-positive rate; prefer conservative confidence thresholds for automatic escalation.
Coordinate with Legal on repository scraping policy; add a suppression list for sensitive namespaces.
Consider later integration with the model-watchtower to seed procurement/partner signals
